title: Why Multi-Agent Systems Are a Cybersecurity Nightmare
takeaways: Deep-Dive into inter-agent trust chains, cascade injections, memory poisoning, and agentic IAM architecture.
Keynote executive threat briefing on AI risk and autonomous ecosystem security by Harsh Verma.

title: The Structural Shift to Autonomous Agent Networks
takeaways: Contrasts legacy single-agent models (bounded execution, explicit human verification, predictable API perimeters) with modern multi-agent systems.
Highlights emergent risks: autonomous collaboration, transitive trust chains where agents implicitly trust peers, and cascading vulnerability surfaces.

title: Multi-Agent Execution Graph Mechanics
takeaways: Traces execution graphs from Node 01 (Retrieval Agent) to Node 02 (Synthesis), Node 03 (Execution), and Node 04 (Validation).
Exploit Pattern: Silent Automated Escalation — poisoned context in ingestion propagates silently across trusted peer nodes without triggering perimeter firewalls.

title: Transitive Trust: The Fundamental Weak Link
takeaways: Implicit payload verification gaps: raw text and JSON pass between sub-agents without cryptographic signatures or schema sanitization.
Unchecked credential inheritance and dynamic topology blind spots prevent runtime proxies from anticipating or enforcing static communication paths.

title: Cascade Prompt Injection & Payload Hopping
takeaways: Step 1 Ingestion Phase: Adversary embeds hidden prompt instructions in untrusted documents or CRM data.
Step 2 Boundary Hopping: Intake agent inadvertently wraps malicious instructions into trusted inter-agent task calls, leading to Step 3 Privilege Execution.

title: Shared Memory & Vector Store Poisoning
takeaways: Corrupting the Collective Brain: Multi-agent systems relying on shared vector databases (Pinecone, Milvus, Redis) face permanent cross-agent context contamination.
Long-term persistence vector lingers across sessions; cross-agent contagion and stealth logic distortion alter decisions without runtime errors.

title: Tool Output Manipulation & API Exploitation
takeaways: Web search tampering hijacks automated research agents via maliciously crafted public web content.
Third-party API poisoning and recursive loop exhaustion can trigger infinite execution loops, spiking cloud API costs and causing complete denial of service.

title: Stanford & UC Berkeley Benchmark Findings
takeaways: Empirical research demonstrates 82% of inter-agent calls accept peer inputs without schema validation or sanitization.
Finding 01: Zero foundation model failure required (underlying LLMs worked within safety bounds; breach occurred via peer trust). Finding 02: Injected prompts traveled across up to 4 agent hops.

title: MITRE ATLAS & OWASP Agentic Top 10 Mapping
takeaways: MITRE ATLAS Tactics: AML.T0051 (Prompt Injection via Inter-Agent Handoffs), AML.T0054 (Vector/Memory Poisoning), AML.T0058 (Excessive Agency).
OWASP Agentic Risks: LLM01 (Indirect Prompt Injection Cascades), LLM06 (Excessive Agency in Sub-Tasks), LLM08 (Unsanitized Memory Poisoning).

title: The Identity Crisis: Traditional IAM vs. Agentic IAM
takeaways: Traditional IAM was built for humans logging into applications; Agentic IAM must govern autonomous software acting on behalf of humans.
Shifts from static RBAC and long-lived OAuth tokens to machine-to-machine delegated authority tokens, task-bound ephemeral scopes, and continuous intent provenance.

title: Machine-to-Machine Identity Delegation Protocol
takeaways: Phase 01 Root Intent Scoping: Human user request mints a cryptographically signed Root Intent Token defining explicit boundary parameters.
Phase 02 Sub-Task Attestation: Orchestrator mints short-lived (60s) downstream tokens; Phase 03: Target API validates caller identity and human intent provenance.

title: Inter-Agent Firewalls & Schema Contracts
takeaways: Strict typed JSON contracts replace raw natural language inter-agent handoffs with strictly validated schemas.
Inline behavioral proxies act as inspection sidecars to detect indirect injections; trust decay algorithms automatically reduce permissions as handoff depth increases.

title: Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) Policy Enforcement
takeaways: Critical Gate Triggers: Mandatory human approval required for state deletions, database modifications, or wire transactions.
Confidence thresholds pause automated execution when uncertainty drops below 95%; immutable audit logs record execution graphs for forensic analysis.

title: CISO Strategic AI Defense Roadmap
takeaways: Phase 01: Asset Discovery & Graph Mapping; Phase 02: Schema Contract Hardening across inter-agent communications.
Phase 03: Agentic IAM Token Deployment with root intent signatures; Phase 04: Inline Telemetry and HITL Gates on write APIs.

title: Protecting Autonomous Machines from Other Machines
takeaways: Executive takeaway: The next major frontier in cybersecurity is protecting machines from other machines operating inside a trusted ecosystem.
RSAC Executive Briefing conclusion and strategic recommendations for autonomous AI resilience.
